breadcrumb.name: 1 Kanal Solar System: Size for a House with 3 to 4 ACs

sections.h2: What is the load of a 1 kanal house?
p: A 1 kanal house usually has four or five bedrooms, a drawing room, a lounge, a large kitchen, servant quarters and a lawn with its own water pump, and most rooms have an AC. The default list is a summer afternoon in such a house: eight ceiling fans, twenty-four LED bulbs, an inverter fridge, a deep freezer, two large TVs, three 1.5 ton inverter ACs in the bedrooms, a 2 ton inverter AC in the lounge, a 1.5 hp water pump, an iron, an automatic washing machine, a microwave, a WiFi router and a CCTV recorder. Together they come to 11,888 W running, 52.2 units a day and about 1,635 units a month.

Four ACs are most of the running load and most of the summer units, so they decide the panels (from the daily units, 13.08 kW) and, with a battery, the hybrid inverter (from the running load). Panels big enough to carry all four ACs at once at midday would need 15.24 kW and make more units than the house uses; that rule is for off-grid systems. If some ACs run only a few hours, enter those hours; if they never run together, a hybrid inverter can be smaller.

sections.h2: How many kW solar for a 1 kanal house with 4 ACs?
p: For the typical house above the answer is 13.46 kW of panels with an inverter of 12 kW: 23 panels of 585 W on about 59 square metres of roof. A 1 kanal roof normally has that space, but water tanks, the stair tower and the parapet shadow in the morning can cut the usable area, so have the installer map the roof before quoting.

With a fifth AC the array grows to 15.21 kW and the inverter to 12 kW. The reference table below runs the same house from no AC to five ACs and to non-inverter ACs, so you can read off the size for the rooms you actually cool.

sections.h2: Is a 15 kW solar system right for a 1 kanal house?
p: A system in the fifteen kW class fits the default house: three 1.5 ton and one 2 ton inverter ACs with the usual fans, lights, kitchen and pump loads come to 13.46 kW of panels and an inverter of 12 kW. An on-grid inverter is sized from the panels (at least the panel kW ÷ 1.3); a hybrid inverter that carries the whole house in a power cut would need 14.86 kW, so with a battery most owners put only the night loads on it.

A system of this size is not a bigger 5 marla system. The inverter is three-phase, the array splits into several strings on more than one MPPT input, the DC cables and breakers are heavier, and the structure has to handle wind load over a large area. Compare quotes on these items, not only on the panel count.

Do not put every panel in one string. On a cold morning each 585 W panel gives about 55 V open-circuit, so 23 panels in series would be about 1,274 V; split them into strings that each stay below the inverter's maximum DC input voltage on its datasheet.

sections.h2: Three-phase connection, sanctioned load and the net billing cap
p: A running load of 11,888 W is far above what a single-phase connection is meant to carry, so a 1 kanal house with four ACs is normally on a three-phase 400 V supply, and the solar inverter must be three-phase too so that the house load and the export are balanced across the phases. A single-phase inverter on a three-phase house can only feed one phase and leaves the other two on the grid.

Your DISCO approves net billing only up to the sanctioned load, so the sanctioned load must be at least the system size; apply for a load extension first if it is lower. Any sanctioned load of 5 kW or more is on a time-of-use meter, which bills peak-hour units at a higher rate. The net billing calculator shows what the export credit is worth against those rates.

sections.h2: Battery for a 1 kanal house: ACs at night or not
p: A grid-tied system needs no battery. For load-shedding backup the battery field sizes a lithium bank for everything in the list, which for four ACs is a bank nobody installs at home. The third and fourth worked examples list the night loads only, once with two bedroom ACs and once without.

With two 1.5 ton inverter ACs, fans, lights, fridge, freezer, one TV, router and CCTV for 6 hours, the bank is about 667 Ah at 48 V (32 units). Without the ACs it is about 219 Ah (10.5 units). Many 1 kanal owners put the bedroom ACs on the battery and leave the lounge AC on the grid at night; the list lets you price both choices.

sections.h2: What does a 1 kanal solar system cost?
p: An on-grid system of this size (13.46 kW of panels with a three-phase inverter of 12 kW, no battery) costs about Rs 1,260,000 to Rs 1,610,000 (Rs 12.6 lakh to Rs 16.1 lakh) installed, from the installer price lists and reports checked on 14 October 2026. Check today's range with the solar system price calculator, ask for complete quotes in Rs per watt of panels, price the battery separately by its units, and test a quote with the solar quote checker. Month-to-month changes are in this month's solar prices.

A complete quote includes the panels, the three-phase inverter, the mounting structure, DC and AC cables, string breakers and surge protection, earthing, installation labour, the net billing application and the three-phase bidirectional meter. Prices for a system this size are often quoted with and without the structure, so check that line.
For other house sizes see the 5 marla solar system and the 10 marla solar system.

faq.q: How many solar panels does a 1 kanal house need?
faq.a: The typical 1 kanal house above needs 23 panels of 585 W, which is 13.46 kW on about 59 square metres of roof. With five inverter ACs it needs 26 panels.

faq.q: What size solar system does a 1 kanal house with 4 ACs need?
faq.a: With three 1.5 ton and one 2 ton inverter ACs plus fans, lights, fridge, freezer, pump and kitchen loads, the house needs 13.46 kW of panels and a three-phase inverter of 12 kW, which makes about 1,635 units a month in Lahore.

faq.q: Is a 15 kW solar system enough for a 1 kanal house?
faq.a: Yes for four inverter ACs with the usual house loads, which need 13.46 kW of panels and an inverter of 12 kW. Five ACs, an electric geyser or non-inverter ACs move the house to a larger size; see the reference table.

faq.q: Does a 1 kanal solar system need a three-phase inverter?
faq.a: Almost always. A running load of 11,888 W is carried by a three-phase 400 V connection, and the inverter must be three-phase so that the house load and the exported units are balanced across all three phases.

faq.q: How many units does a 1 kanal solar system make a month?
faq.a: About 1,635 units a month for the 13.46 kW system in Lahore as a yearly average, against about 52.2 units a day used in summer. Summer months make more, winter months less; pick your city for its own sun yield.

faq.q: Can the solar system run the ACs at night?
faq.a: Only from a battery or from the grid. Two 1.5 ton inverter ACs with fans, lights, fridge, freezer and CCTV for 6 hours need about 667 Ah of lithium at 48 V; without the ACs the night needs about 219 Ah. Most owners run one or two bedroom ACs from the battery and the rest from the grid.

faq.q: What is the price of a 1 kanal solar system?
faq.a: About Rs 1,260,000 to Rs 1,610,000 installed for a 13.46 kW on-grid system with no battery, from price lists checked on 14 October 2026. Compare quotes in Rs per watt for the complete system with a three-phase inverter of 12 kW, including structure, cables, protection, installation and the net billing application, price the battery separately, and check a quote with the solar quote checker.

key_facts: A typical 1 kanal house with four inverter ACs (three 1.5 ton and one 2 ton) has a running load of about 11,888 W and uses about 52.2 units a day, so it needs a solar system of about 13.46 kW with an inverter of 12 kW.
A fifth AC (four 1.5 ton and one 2 ton inverter ACs) raises the same house to about 15.21 kW of panels (26 panels) and an inverter of 12 kW.
The 13.46 kW array needs about 59 square metres of unshaded roof at 585 W per panel and makes about 1,635 units a month in Lahore as a yearly average.

A load of this size is normally on a three-phase 400 V connection with a sanctioned load well above 5 kW, so the inverter is three-phase, the house is on a time-of-use meter, and the net billing cap equals the sanctioned load.

Running two 1.5 ton inverter ACs with fans, lights, fridge, freezer and CCTV for 6 hours after sunset needs a lithium battery of about 667 Ah at 48 V (32 units); without the ACs the same night needs about 219 Ah.
mistakes: Fitting a single-phase inverter to a three-phase house. It feeds one phase only; the other two phases keep buying from the grid and the export is limited to that one phase.
Entering every AC at full-day hours. The panels follow the daily units, so an AC used for a few hours should be entered with those hours; the ACs that run together set a hybrid inverter.
Applying for net billing before the load extension. The DISCO caps the system at the sanctioned load, so a 13.46 kW array on a small sanctioned load is refused or cut down.
Sizing the battery for the whole list. For four ACs that is a bank nobody fits at home; list the night loads only and decide which ACs, if any, run on the battery.
Ignoring roof shade. Twenty-plus panels need about 59 square metres clear of the water tank, the stair tower and the parapet shadow; a shaded string drags down the whole MPPT input it is on.

A grid-tied or hybrid system is sized by energy: when the {{out.running_w|int}} W running load is more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the rest. {{out.kw|2}} kW needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w}} W = {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW installed on about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof, making about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month. {{out.inverter_text}}
how.text: Energy: watts × quantity × hours a day for each appliance (inverter ACs count at their average draw, not their rated watts), added up = 52.2 units a day; ÷ 4 units per kW of panels a day in your city = 13.08 kW. A grid-tied or hybrid system is sized by energy: when the 11,888 W running load is more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the rest. 13.08 kW needs 23 panels of 585 W = 13.46 kW installed on about 59 square metres of roof, making about 1,635 units a month. Inverter: an on-grid inverter runs beside the grid, which starts motors and covers any shortfall, so it is sized by the panels: 13.46 kW ÷ 1.3 = at least 10.35 kW, so the on-grid inverter to buy is 12 kW; no surge rating is needed.

examples.title: Typical 1 kanal house with four inverter ACs
examples.text: Eight fans, twenty-four bulbs, inverter fridge, deep freezer, two large TVs, three 1.5 ton and one 2 ton inverter ACs, 1.5 hp pump, iron, washing machine, microwave, router and CCTV: 11,888 W running and 52.2 units a day. Solar system 13.46 kW (23 panels, about 59 square metres), inverter 12 kW, about 1,635 units a month.

examples.title: 1 kanal house with five inverter ACs
examples.text: The same house with a fourth 1.5 ton inverter AC in the guest room: 13,338 W running and 60.2 units a day. Solar system 15.21 kW (26 panels), inverter 12 kW, about 1,848 units a month. One more AC adds about three panels of 585 W.

examples.title: Night loads with two bedroom ACs: battery for 6 hours
examples.text: Only the night loads are listed: eight fans, twenty-four bulbs, fridge, freezer, one TV, router, CCTV and two 1.5 ton inverter ACs, 4,318 W. For 6 hours after sunset the battery must hold 25.9 units, about 667 Ah at 48 V using 90% of a lithium bank (32 units rated). The panels for the whole house come from the first example, not from this list.

examples.title: Night loads without ACs: battery for 6 hours
examples.text: Fans, bulbs, fridge, freezer, one TV, router and CCTV only, 1,418 W. For 6 hours the battery must hold 8.5 units, about 219 Ah at 48 V (10.5 units rated). Keeping the ACs on the grid at night cuts the battery to a third of the previous example.

content.answer: A typical 1 kanal house with four inverter ACs, eight fans, lights, an inverter fridge, a deep freezer, two large TVs, a 1.5 hp water pump and kitchen appliances needs a solar system of about 13.46 kW (23 panels) with a three-phase on-grid inverter of 12 kW. Panels = daily units ÷ sun yield; the grid covers the moments when everything runs at once.

formula.text: kW = E_day ÷ yield (grid-tied or hybrid; P_run ÷ 1000 ÷ PR is the off-grid rule, shown for comparison); panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel)
lines: E_day = Σ (watts × qty × hours) ÷ 1000, units used a day
yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city
P_run = total running watts, PR = performance ratio

On-grid inverter W = kW × 1000 ÷ r_max, r_max = largest panel-to-inverter (DC/AC) ratio; hybrid (backup hours set): max(P_run × margin, kW × 1000 ÷ r_max), surge ≥ largest starting load; then the next size sold
Battery Ah = P_run × night hours ÷ (V × DoD × η)

content.safety: A three-phase solar system connects to the grid and to the house wiring at 400 V, and its DC strings run at several hundred volts; have a licensed electrician and a AEDB-certified installer do the wiring, earthing, surge protection and the net billing connection, and never work on the DC side with the strings connected.
